question: Can a genuinely repeated native attention layer supply a causal neural-cache distribution that improves held-out raw language prediction and efficiency over untouched Base?
protocol: Pinned ordinary Qwen Base reference. Candidate quantizes eligible Base weights outside final layer 23 to 8-bit groups of 64, then executes that native layer twice at stabilized alpha .35. First-pass native probabilities remain a distribution over the entire vocabulary. Dot products of normalized second-pass decoder representations key a 256-entry causal memory of previously observed tokens. Learn only log-temperature, interpolation intercept and similarity slope using next-token likelihood on 96 WikiText-2 train articles (256 targets each). Compare against 40 distinct WikiText-2 test articles (10240 targets) plus the original 120 disjoint prose, scientific and documentation passages (9328 targets). Each row starts with empty memory. For every prediction at index t only earlier states j<t can vote for tokens j+1. Identical IDs, no answer format or lookahead, full-vocabulary top-1, per-token NLL, measured time including both native passes and vocabulary projection, warm MLX peak. Greedily generate on the first six true prefixes without seeing future tokens in a separate incremental path and require parity with scored top-1.
gate: At least .015 nats/token lower aggregate NLL on each corpus, no more than .02 worse on any original retention domain, no lower top-1 counts on either corpus and strictly positive pooled top-1 gain. More WikiText articles improved with exact two-sided article sign p<=.05. Require no greater warmed pooled time or peak memory, and six correct prefix-parity checks. Failure closes default raw-language promotion for this configuration. Passing licenses an equal-calibration native one-pass cache comparison and independent unseen document replication before deployment.
